phase3_findings.description: src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py lines 177-184: an unexpected parser exception (anything but ParseError/TokenError, e.g. RecursionError or a sqlglot dialect-parser bug) now makes is_introspection_query return True, so _format.py (lines 386-395, 418-419) withholds a genuine data result while the turn returns isError false; only a server-side WARNING records it. The broad except also hides AttributeError/KeyError/TypeError programming errors. test_unexpected_parser_error_fails_closed pins the True return; no test covers what the client sees.

src/sqllens/tools/_format.py lines 386-395: the INFO 'withheld a schema-introspection run_sql result' log fires only when _build_table_payload returns a payload, so the payload-failure case is not logged as withheld (the payload-failure WARNING still fires).

docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md line 102: 'each withheld result logs INFO server-side' is broader than the code; _format.py lines 386-420 log the withheld INFO only when _build_table_payload returns a payload. Capped at Suggestion by the behavior-inert prose cap.

src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py lines 67-93: each _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT key must be a URL-scheme prefix, a sqlglot dialect name and a catalog entry at once; an engine whose scheme differs from its sqlglot name (mssql/tsql) cannot be described, an engine added without a catalog entry silently gives the guards dialect=None, and prefix matching relies on dict order and non-overlapping keys in a mutable module-level dict. No production path affected today.

src/sqllens/tools/_format.py lines 389-434: last_sql_is_introspection stays set until the next run_sql card, so any later DataFrame is withheld whatever produced it; only RunSqlTool emits DataFrames today, so unreachable now.
